## Visualization

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// EXAMPLE DATA (made up) - replace with your own
data = [
  {year: 2019, rate: 12.1},
  {year: 2020, rate: 11.4},
  {year: 2021, rate: 10.8},
  {year: 2022, rate: 9.9},
  {year: 2023, rate: 9.2}
]
Plot.plot({
  title: "Example data: readmission rate (%) by year",
  y: {grid: true, label: "Rate (%)", domain: [0, 14]},
  x: {label: "Year", tickFormat: "d"},
  marks: [
    Plot.barY(data, {x: "year", y: "rate", fill: "steelblue"}),
    Plot.ruleY([0])
  ]
})
```

NOTE: To use R or Python instead of OJS (requires R or Python + Jupyter installed),
replace the ojs chunk above with a chunk whose language is r or python
(write the opening fence as three backticks followed by {r} or {python}),
for example in R: library(ggplot2); ggplot(df, aes(year, rate)) + geom_col()
or in Python: import matplotlib.pyplot as plt; plt.bar(years, rates)
